m: Om. One should meditate on Durga, known as Jaya, dark as a black cloud, giving fear to the hosts of enemies by her sidelong glances, a streak of the moon bound in her crown, bearing in her hands a conch, a discus, a sword, and a trident, three-eyed, mounted on the shoulder of a lion, filling all the three worlds with her splendour,
surrounded by the gods and served by those who desire success. Om. The seer said:

When that exceedingly valiant evil-minded one had been slain by the Goddess, and the army of the gods' enemies as well, the hosts of gods beginning with Shakra praised her, their necks and shoulders bent in reverence, their bodies beautiful with the rising of hair from great joy.

To the Goddess by whose own power this world is spread, whose form is the gathered power of the entire host of gods, to Ambika, worshipped by all gods and great seers, we bow with devotion. May she appoint auspicious things for us.

Her unequalled majesty the blessed Ananta, Brahma, and Hara are not able to declare, nor her strength. May Chandika set her mind on the protection of the whole world and on the destruction of the fear of what is inauspicious.

She who is herself Shri in the houses of those who do good, Alakshmi in the hearts of the sinful, intelligence in the hearts of the wise, faith among the good, and modesty in one born of a good family: we bow to you. Protect the universe, Goddess.

How shall we describe this form of yours, which cannot be conceived? And how this abundant, exceedingly valiant power that destroys asuras? And how these deeds of yours in battles, which are beyond all, among all the hosts of asuras and gods and the rest, Goddess?

You are the cause of all the worlds. Though you are the three qualities, you are not known by their faults, even by Hari, Hara, and the others. You are shoreless. All this world, which has become a part, rests on you. You are the supreme unmanifest nature, the first.

By the uttering of whom all the gods, in all the sacrifices, reach satisfaction, Goddess, you are svaha. And you are the cause of satisfaction for the hosts of ancestors. Therefore people pronounce you as svadha.

You, whose great vow cannot be conceived, are the cause of liberation. You are practised by those whose senses are well restrained and who have the essence of reality, by sages seeking release, all their faults cast away. You are that knowledge, blessed one, the supreme, Goddess.

You consist of sound. You are the treasury of the very pure Rig and Yajus, and of the Samans, which have the beautiful recitation of the udgitha. Goddess, the blessed three Vedas, you are the livelihood of all the worlds, for the sake of worldly life, the destroyer of the highest pain.

You are intelligence, Goddess, known as the essence of all the scriptures. You are Durga, a boat without attachment on the hard ocean of worldly life. You are Shri, whose one dwelling was made in the heart of the enemy of Kaitabha. You yourself are Gauri, whose foundation was made by him whose crown is the moon.

Your face, with a slight smile, spotless, resembling the orb of the full moon, lovely with the lustre of the finest gold, is exceedingly wonderful. Even so, Mahishasura, seized by anger, suddenly looked upon it when it was struck.

And seeing, Goddess, that angry face made gaping by the frown, rising with a lustre like the moon, that Mahisha did not at once give up his life. That is very strange. For who lives after seeing an angry Death?

Goddess, be gracious. You are supreme for worldly life, and when angry you at once destroy families. This has just now been understood, that this very abundant army of Mahishasura has been brought to its end.

Those with whom you are pleased have wealth in their countries, their renown does not sink, and their band of kinsmen does not fail. They alone are fortunate, with children, servants, and wife at peace, you who always give rise when you are gracious.

Goddess, the doer of good, highly honoured, always performs all the rightful acts every day, and then by your grace goes to heaven. By that, Goddess, you are the giver of fruit even in the three worlds.

Durga, when remembered you take away the fear of every creature. Remembered by those who are well, you give a very auspicious understanding. Remover of poverty, sorrow, and fear, who other than you is always tender-hearted for the sake of doing good to all?

By these being slain the world obtains happiness, and yet, thinking, Let them do evil for a long time, for hell, and let them reach heaven by attaining death in battle, you surely slay the hostile, Goddess.

Why do you not reduce all the asuras to ashes at the mere sight of them, you who send weapons against enemies? Let even enemies go to the worlds purified by weapons. Such a good intention toward those hostile ones arises in you.

That the eyes of the asuras were not brought to dissolution by the fierce flashes of the mass of your sword's light, and by the flood of light from the tip of your spear, while they looked on your face, worthy of the rays of the moon: this is that wonder.

Your conduct, Goddess, is the quieting of the conduct of the badly behaved. And this form of yours cannot be conceived and is unequal to others. And your valour destroys those who robbed the gods of their prowess. Even toward enemies, compassion is thus shown by you.

What could be a comparison for this prowess of yours? And where is a form that takes away the fear and the pain caused by enemies? Tenderness in the heart, and harshness set on battle, are seen in you alone, Goddess, giver of boons, even in the three worlds.

This whole triple world has been protected by you through the destruction of the foe. Having slain them too at the forefront of the battle, you have led the enemy hosts to heaven, and our fear, born of the raging enemy of the gods, has been driven off. Salutation to you.
Protect us with the spear, Goddess. Protect us with the sword, Ambika. Protect us with the sound of the bell, and with the sound of the bowstring.
Guard us in the east and in the west, Chandika. Guard us in the south, and in the north, sovereign, by the whirling of your own spear.
With those gentle forms of yours that move in the triple world, and with those that are exceedingly terrible, protect us and the earth.
With those weapons of yours, Ambika, sword, spear, mace, and the rest, which rest in your hands that are tender as young shoots, protect us on every side.
The seer said:
Praised in this way by the gods, she was worshipped with divine flowers grown in Nandana, the supporter of the worlds, and with scented unguents.
Well incensed with divine incenses by all the gods, with devotion, she, her face gracious, spoke to all the gods who had bowed.
The Goddess said:
Choose, all you gods, whatever you desire from me.
The gods said:
Everything has been done by the blessed one. Nothing remains to be done.
Since this enemy of ours, Mahishasura, has been slain. But if a boon is still to be given by you to us, great sovereign,
remembered, remembered, may you destroy our supreme calamities. And the mortal who praises you with these hymns, O you of spotless face,
for the increase of his wealth, prosperity, riches, wife, and other good fortune, may you, gracious to us, be so, giver of all, Ambika.
The seer said:
Thus entreated by the gods for the sake of the world and for their own sake, Bhadrakali said, So be it, and vanished, O king.
Thus it has been told, O king, how she arose of old, the Goddess, from the bodies of the gods, seeking the welfare of the three worlds.
And again, how she arose from the body of Gauri, for the slaying of wicked daityas, and of Shumbha and Nishumbha,
and for the protection of the worlds, doing good to the gods: hear that. I will tell it to you properly, as it is told by me.
